Sample.evidence_source: The total score of the BAS-2 was significantly higher in men compared with women, t(1031) = 2.37, p = .021. A univariate analysis of variance showed that there was no significant between-group difference in body appreciation, F(6, 1025) = 0.69, p = .660. The degrees of freedom for the t-test (1031) implies N-1, so N=1032. The degrees of freedom for the ANOVA (1025) implies N-k-1, where k=6, so N=1025+6+1=1032. Thus, the total sample size is 1032.

Source of sample.evidence_source: The mean score of the BAS-2 was also compared across universities. This indicates the sample was drawn from universities.

Assessment of BA.evidence_source: In addition, the total score of the BAS-2 was significantly higher in men compared with women.

Number of studies.evidence_source: The text describes a single study comparing BAS-2 scores between men and women and across universities, not multiple distinct studies.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details between-group differences in Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) scores. It reports item-level comparisons and total BAS-2 scores between men and women, finding men had significantly higher total BAS-2 scores. Additionally, it examines BAS-2 scores across universities, finding no significant differences.
section_summary.evidence_source: The section discusses item-level comparisons between men and women for 10 items, and the total score of the BAS-2 between men and women, and also across universities.
